official_measurement_examples.name: FRA trigger scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance updated 28 May 2026 requires an FRA for specified development in Flood Zones 2, 3 and 3b and for several Flood Zone 1 risk cases, including sites of 1 hectare or more and mapped future or surface-water risk cases.

official_measurement_examples.name: Flood Zone probabilities
official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2026 Flood Zones dataset defines present-day river and sea probability bands and states Flood Zone 1 is the land outside mapped Zones 2 and 3.

official_measurement_examples.name: Climate-change layer role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Flood Zones plus Climate Change is a composite screening dataset intended to help identify the need for an FRA and sequential test; it assumes no future changes to defences or land use.

official_measurement_examples.name: Surface-water spatial limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The July 2026 surface-water planning extents indicate area-level flood risk and explicitly are not suitable for determining whether an individual property is at risk.

official_measurement_examples.name: Unsatisfactory FRA consequence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency planning guidance states an LPA may refuse an application if a required FRA is missing or unsatisfactory; a mapped zone alone is not the final planning decision.

official_measurement_examples.name: SFRA role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local planning authorities should prepare strategic flood risk assessments for their area and the May 2026 guidance requires consideration of mapped risk from all sources and climate change.

official_measurement_examples.name: Map terms limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Flood Map for Planning service provides planning risk information and downloadable maps but states displayed material is supplied without guarantees as to accuracy, so site-specific appraisal can still be required.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Flood mapping, an FRA, sequential or exception testing, drainage strategy and any other watercourse permits are separate controls and do not themselves establish land ownership or parcel development capacity.

core_rules: Flood Zone geometry is screening evidence not a complete planning decision
Flood Zone 1 is not proof of zero flood risk
Flood Zones plus Climate Change must not be treated as present-day probability geometry
surface-water planning extents are not individual-property flood determinations
an FRA requirement is not automatic planning refusal
a completed FRA is not planning permission
sequential-test evidence is distinct from exception-test evidence
SFRA evidence is strategic and must not silently replace site-specific assessment
existing flood defences must not be assumed to eliminate residual risk
historic flood outlines must retain date source and model context
drainage strategy is distinct from flood-zone classification
Environment Agency consultation is not land ownership or access authority
flood-risk compliance does not reserve development capacity
map-service output must retain dataset limitations and update date
no parcel flood clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
